newsitem.title: FRANCE: Kohl says in no rush to decide on seeking re-election.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says in no rush to decide on seeking re-election.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Sunday that he was in no hurry to decide whether to stand for re-election in 1998 and that, when the time came, he would do his duty and examine his conscience.

Asked about an opinion poll published last week which showed 55 percent of Germans did not want him to run again, Kohl told French TF1 television channel in an interview: "Of course I don't believe this poll...The second point is: I have not made my mind up. I'm not evading the question."

Kohl drew fire over the weekend as Herbert Mai, the head of Germany's OeTV, the public sector service workers' union, blamed his government for Germany's record-high jobless rate, and politicians said he was incapable of solving the problem.
Germany reported this week that its unemployment rate had climbed in January from December's 10.8 percent to 12.2 percent, or 4.66 million -- the highest level since 1933.

Day in day out, Kohl said, he had to work harder than almost anyone. "And I'm now at a time of life where I do indeed ask myself: 'What's the smart thing to do? What can you still change? What use are you still?'

"And I'm quite calm about that, and I'll take my decision quite calmly...I want to do my duty, and I will have to examine my own conscience and decide for myself in conversation with my closest relatives, with my family and my political friends. And this conversation doesn not have to take place yet," he said.
